clue.text: Form of life apt to be seen in shabby theatre?

indicators.note: a new form of the words means their letters are moulded into another shape

explanation.surface: A biology question: some living creature apt to turn up in a run-down cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' asks for the letters of LIFE APT rearranged; the surface hints that an insect is the life form found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dingy, cheap cinema or theatre, supposedly infested with insects.

clue.text: Load of soldiers involved in campaign

indicators.note: the soldiers are wrapped up inside the word for campaign, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to campaign is to fight for a cause
RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Military logistics: the baggage carried by troops on campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo or goods carried by a vehicle make up its load.

clue.text: Look, it's not good for you

definitions.text: Look, it's not good for you

parts.note: evil is the opposite of good
an eye is a look, as in 'cast an eye over'

explanation.surface: A warning glance, said with a wagged finger: this is bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a malevolent glance believed to bring harm, while its parts give the two words in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A glare superstitiously thought to cast a curse on whoever receives it.

parts.note: describes a song of praise or victory, originally a Greek hymn addressed to Apollo

explanation.definitionFit: A song of thanksgiving or exultation, in ancient Greece sung to Apollo the healer.

parts.note: a title is a legal claim or right, as to property
a page is a boy servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A boy asserts his right to have written some book.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book bearing its name and author, a standard part of a printed work.

clue.text: Give assistance to gull, we hear?

indicators.note: says the word is to be taken by how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a gull is a dupe, someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Should you help a seabird? Apparently so, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' looks like the bird, but it is the verb's noun sense of an easily fooled person.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring aid or relief to someone in difficulty.

indicators.note: the point is caught and held inside the word for screen

parts.note: to screen is to sift, as with sand or applicants
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A sharp tip grabbed by a screenwriter, as if in a film-studio scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen writer' reads as one word, screenwriter; split it, and 'screen' is the verb sift.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, Irish satirist and author of Gulliver's Travels.

parts.note: to train someone is to coach them
to travel round is to tour

explanation.surface: A vacation spent travelling by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' reads as the railway, but it is the verb meaning instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip by bus visiting several places, taken as a vacation.

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
rotund means plump and round

explanation.surface: A dizzy circular chant going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a voice that is full and resonant, or a style that is rich and pompous, rounded in tone.

parts.note: embarrassment turns one red in the face
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax counted by heads

explanation.surface: A girl is flustered by a survey of opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' suggests a vote; here it is the archaic word for the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with red hair, here standing in for any girl.

clue.text: Urgent information in way out setting

indicators.note: the information goes inside the word for way out, which serves as its setting

parts.note: an exit is a way out
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Pressing details displayed on an emergency exit sign.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British slang for information; 'setting' links, saying the exit frames it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding immediate attention; pressing.

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the letters struggle and wrestle out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: A tired person struggling forward, described in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges I (One) and ONWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning in short, to sum up concisely.

clue.text: Sector that's not ripe for development

definitions.text: Sector that's not ripe for development

parts.words: Sector that's not ripe for development
parts.note: reads as unripe produce, but means a zone of countryside protected from building

explanation.definitionFit: A ring of open land around a town where planning law restricts construction.
Means both a noble lineage and the spectators filling a theatre.

parts.note: a tie is a bond or connection
up means over or expired, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A guaranteed bond that has expired.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or make fast, as a boat at a mooring.

parts.note: to pocket something is to take it dishonestly

indicators.note: the word is left just short of complete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: entire means full or complete

explanation.surface: A thief takes nearly the whole sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last L from FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: As much as a pocket will hold, a quantity.

clue.text: Ran, unfortunately turning out bad second

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, unluckily rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A race report: a runner unluckily finished a poor second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' looks like racing, but it means fled; the letters of BAD SECOND are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled secretly, escaping from custody or duty.

definitions.meaning: fulfilled, as a requirement or demand that has been met

explanation.surface: A polite greeting: delighted to make your acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both contented and fulfilled, as a condition or demand.

indicators.note: treating the letters handles them in a new way, reworking their order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A doctor's verdict that the care given to a sick patient was poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges I (one) and INFECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking in some necessary quality; insufficient.

clue.text: Determined group's to have late start

indicators.note: the word for late comes at the start, before the group

parts.note: late means deceased, as in 'the late king'
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A team insists on beginning after the scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy; it goes at the start of SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly resolved, fixed in intention.

indicators.note: the article pokes into the composer's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Gabriel Faure was a French composer
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian piece of writing investigates why a composer's work failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests journalism; here it is the grammatical word 'the' in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete lack of success; a fiasco.

definitions.meaning: Uncle ..., narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's folk tales
the twin who, with Romulus, founded Rome in legend

explanation.surface: Someone's relative turns out to be a civic dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the storyteller uncle in American folk tales and of a legendary co-founder of Rome.

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree
under means subject to, as in under orders

explanation.surface: A lecturer's topic that makes the listener talk aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks like a field of study; it means under, as in subject to.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk or wander in a rambling, aimless way.

clue.text: Poet reportedly like Crabbe, we hear?

indicators.note: says the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a crab has a shell, so being like one is shelly

explanation.surface: A poet compared to fellow poet George Crabbe.
explanation.walkthrough: Crabbe was a real English poet, steering toward comparison of verse; but read as 'crab', having a shell. 'we hear' repeats the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley, English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Herb supplied by nurseryman is expensive

indicators.note: the letters are provided from within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A gardener's shop charges a lot for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb sits inside nurserymAN IS Expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic plant whose seeds taste of liquorice.

clue.text: Outclass European sporting venture that's hopeless

indicators.note: sporting suggests playing about, so the letters frolic into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Trying to beat a European team at sport is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' rearranges OUTCLASS and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaking with no chance of success.

indicators.note: say signals the word as spoken, matching in sound but spelt differently

parts.note: a person who guides leads

explanation.surface: Campus tour guides, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in northern England with a university.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of Leeds, a large English university.

parts.note: Sergeant Cuff is the detective in Wilkie Collins's novel The Moonstone

explanation.surface: A police officer handed little containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' is the verb: to strike, as in boxing someone's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits with the open hand, as one might box ears.

clue.text: Brush with the French results in brawl

parts.note: to brush against is to scuff, graze lightly
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A skirmish with French forces ends in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused, disorderly fight.

clue.text: Popular female lied about being unbeliever

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman fibbed about her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED as IDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rejects a religion; a non-believer.

definitions.meaning: a frame on which climbing plants grow
a lattice or grid of crossing strips

explanation.surface: Mountaineering backup provided by a team of contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice framework, holding up climbing plants and forming a criss-cross mesh.

indicators.note: the monarch leaves the vessel, taken out of its word

parts.note: a destroyer is a warship
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A king or queen leaving a vessel, which is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth; it leaves DESTROYER.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin completely; demolish.
